target_customer: Fintech and investing apps that need to connect users' retail brokerage accounts for data and trading
problem: Bank-focused aggregators offer limited investment support and no trading, so developers cannot easily read or trade in users' existing brokerage accounts.
product_category: Brokerage account aggregation and trading API

founders.name: Brendan Lee Young
founders.role: Founder and CEO of parent Passiv
founders.background_notes: YC page: from Trinidad and Tobago, based in Canada, previously a DJ and party promoter.

founders.name: Brendan Wood
founders.background_notes: YC page: robotics engineer in software and high-performance computing, based in New Brunswick. A Benzinga item calls him SnapTrade's CEO and a search result says he built SnapTrade.

competitors.name: Plaid and other bank-focused aggregators
competitors.what: Aggregators focused on bank accounts with limited investment support and no trading; the YC tagline is Plaid for trading

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalising dozens of brokerage connections, many without public APIs, is laborious integration work with security needs.

defensibility.rationale: Broker integrations and partner relationships take years to build and developers embed the API, but Plaid could extend its investment product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Plaid Investments remains read-only per comparison write-ups; SnapTrade remains independent, acquired Wealthly via parent Passiv, and partnered with Webull in December 2025.

market_need_then: The seed announcement said 20+ investing apps already used SnapTrade and that the parent Passiv had run a consumer app for five years to learn developers' needs.

identity.visual_style: Developer API marketing with comparison pages

branding.community_and_virality: Partner announcements with Webull, Public and Tickblaze, plus a Benzinga profile; no consumer community.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear name and a strong analogy tagline, but a B2B infrastructure brand with limited public brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: SnapTrade is the B2B product of Passiv, a Fredericton fintech founded in 2017, and it reached YC in Winter 2022 after Passiv's consumer app taught it what developers needed. It raised a 2.2 million dollar seed in October 2022 and grew to 17 people, and reports that it facilitated data access for over a million accounts in 2025. Later investment from TLT East Ventures was undisclosed.
notes: The seed was raised by Passiv for SnapTrade; the press release was read via Newswire and cross-checked by FinTech Futures, Fintech.ca and Seedtable search listings. Brendan Wood is described as CEO by Benzinga and a search summary but the YC page says Founder; titles unverified. 2025 investment from TLT East Ventures is undisclosed (June or July 2025) and is not recorded as a round. CB Insights shows $500K total and Caplight $3M, aggregator only. The Plaid competitor entry cites a release that does not name Plaid; Plaid is named in the YC tagline. Outcome search found no shutdown.
